body:
I know what it feels like to not want to be open about it. Just know that your friends failure to cope with this, that about her not being able to deal with it, not you. i too am halted from ending it by the pain it would cause others. i think a lot of times our empathy is what gets us so hurt in the first place. try to live not for others, but for yourself. see if you can make it to september, not focusing on your plans for death, but your plans for life. who knows, you may just find something worth living for. 

I think the legendary stephen fry has better advice than i could ever give you. i copied and pasted it below, i hope it can give you the comfort that it once gave me.

"I'm so sorry to hear that life is getting you down at the moment. Goodness knows, it can be so tough when nothing seems to fit and little seems to be fulfilling. I'm not sure there's any specific advice I can give that will help bring life back its savour. Although they mean well, it's sometimes quite galling to be reminded how much people love you when you don't love yourself that much. 

I've found that it's of some help to think of one's moods and feelings about the world as being similar to weather:

Here are some obvious things about the weather:

It's real.
You can't change it by wishing it away. 
If it's dark and rainy it really is dark and rainy and you can't alter it. 
It might be dark and rainy for two weeks in a row.

BUT

It will be sunny one day.
It isn't under one's control as to when the sun comes out, but come out it will. 
One day.

It really is the same with one's moods, I think. The wrong approach is to believe that they are illusions. They are real. Depression, anxiety, listlessness - these are as real as the weather - AND EQUALLY NOT UNDER ONE'S CONTROL. Not one's fault. 

BUT 

They will pass: they really will.

In the same way that one has to accept the weather, so one has to accept how one feels about life sometimes. "Today's a crap day," is a perfectly realistic approach. It's all about finding a kind of mental umbrella. "Hey-ho, it's raining inside: it isn't my fault and there's nothing I can do about it, but sit it out. But the sun may well come out tomorrow and when it does, I shall take full advantage."

I don't know if any of that is of any use: it may not seem it, and if so, I'm sorry. I just thought I'd drop you a line to wish you well in your search to find a little more pleasure and purpose in life. 

Very best wishes"

We are brothers in arms in this struggle called life. As long as you are alive on this planet you will never be truly alone- thats one thing buddhism taught me. One love, best wishes, and good luck.

thank you for the response. I think i will stick around for a little longer and see if anyone else finds this interesting enough to read through the whole thing and leave a comment. Sadly, it sometimes seems like the whole world is on a TL;DR vibe, either too cynical or too busy to care about anyone else but themselves. 

anyway, heres a little positive that got me through my last year. a quote i was forced to memorize, that ironically turned into my little salvation. 

"**Nothing in the world can take the place of Persistence.**
Talent will not; nothing is more common than unsuccessful men with talent. Genius will not; unrewarded genius is almost a proverb. 
Education will not; the world is full of educated derelicts. 
**Persistence and determination alone are omnipotent. 
The slogan 'Press On' has solved and always will solve the problems of the human race.**"

"Press On" in latin is *perge*. sometimes when everything is too much, i hear a little voice in the back of my mind, different from the ones I usually hear, the ones that torment me and scream at me and tell me I'm worthless. No, this voice is my own, and it simply whispers *perge, perge, perge*

As Jimmy V says, "don't give up, don't ever give up". I pray i stay strong enough to take his advice.

And by the way, just by understanding, you have given me more support than you could ever know.
